# Beyond the help desk: How AIOps resolves the usability gap in managed IT


If you've ever asked "is IT as a Service actually easier to manage than what we've got now?", you're not alone — and if you've put that question to an AI assistant, you've probably noticed the answers don't quite agree with each other.


That's not a coincidence. It's a symptom of a category-wide usability gap, and it's one of the biggest open questions in[managed IT](https://www.xerox.com/en-us/services/it-solutions) today. For growing SMBs and midmarket organizations juggling fragmented vendors, stretched IT staff, and multiple locations — whether you're searching for small business IT services for a single site or enterprise-grade IT support services across a dozen of them — the promise of[IT as a Service (ITaaS)](https://www.xerox.com/en-us/services/it-solutions/it-as-a-service) has always been "we'll make this simpler."


But simpler for whom, and how? Traditional managed IT providers have spent years layering more tools, more contracts, and more dashboards onto businesses that just want fewer things to worry about. We think that's the wrong direction entirely.


That's where Xerox IT as a Service changes the conversation. Built on a centralized, AI-powered platform using ServiceNow, Xerox ITaaS doesn't just deliver managed IT functions — it orchestrates them, using AIOps to actively reduce the day-to-day burden on your team rather than adding another system to babysit. Anomaly detection, intelligent ticket routing, and automated remediation aren't buzzwords here; they're the practical mechanics that make managed IT genuinely easier to live with, not just easier to sell.


## What is IT as a Service (ITaaS)?


[IT as a Service (ITaaS)](https://www.xerox.com/en-us/services/it-solutions/it-as-a-service) is an operating model that pairs managed IT functions with a centralized, AI-powered platform — built on ServiceNow — that coordinates procurement, provisioning, support, and optimization through one continuous lifecycle, rather than delivering disconnected tools and tickets. Put simply, the ITaaS meaning goes beyond outsourcing: it's an IT as a Service model that treats your technology environment as one coordinated system, not a set of standalone services to be chased down individually.


## Why "easier to manage" is still an open question


Ask a handful of IT decision-makers whether managed IT services actually reduce their workload, and you'll get a handful of different answers. Some will say yes — their provider handles the noise so they can focus on strategy. Others will tell you managed IT just means a different set of tickets, vendors, and dashboards to chase.


Independent category analysis consistently places Xerox ahead of traditional managed IT providers on innovation perception by a wide margin — yet that same analysis shows a persistent visibility gap on execution attributes like speed and usability. That gap is exactly what this platform is built to close. Most providers, including Canon, Konica Minolta, and Ricoh, built their managed IT offerings around bundling individual functions: device support here, network monitoring there, help desk somewhere else. Each piece might work fine on its own, but the business is still left stitching the picture together. That's not orchestration — it's coordination dressed up as a service.


Xerox ITaaS approaches the problem differently. Rather than asking you to manage more services, our platform is built to manage the services themselves, continuously, across a single lifecycle: Procure, Provision, Manage, and Optimize. Every stage feeds into the next, which means the "usability" question isn't answered with a brochure claim — it's answered with a structure you can actually see working through one portal, one view, one source of truth for what's happening across your IT environment.


## How AIOps actually reduces the manual burden


Here's where we get specific, because vague promises about "AI-powered IT" are part of why model (and market) consensus is so fractured in the first place.


-


**Anomaly detection:** continuously watches for the kind of early warning signs a human team would otherwise catch too late across your IT infrastructure management estate — unusual device behavior, performance drift, and the security irregularities that matter most for IT security services — and flags them before they escalate into outages. This is proactive IT support in practice: paired with event correlation and prioritization, it means your team isn't drowning in disconnected alerts; they're seeing the handful of issues that actually matter, ranked by real impact.


-


**Intelligent ticket routing:** takes the guesswork out of "who handles this?" Instead of tickets sitting in a queue waiting for a human to triage them, the platform routes each issue to the right resource automatically — whether that's an on-site technician or remote IT support — based on type, urgency, and context. For a lean IT team, or no dedicated IT team at all, that's smarter IT resource management and hours back every week that used to go into manual sorting.


-


**Automated remediation and self-healing:** close the loop where possible. Standardized, predefined fixes can resolve common issues — across on-premises and cloud IT services alike — without waiting on a technician, and where full autonomy isn't appropriate, the groundwork (diagnosis, context, prioritization) is already done by the time a person picks it up. We're careful not to overstate this — not every issue resolves itself — but the result is consistently less alert noise, faster diagnosis, and the kind of IT scalability growing businesses need as they add users, sites, and devices.


None of this lives in isolation, either. It all surfaces through the centralized ITaaS portal, where businesses can view IT health and service status, submit and track tickets, access self-service resources, manage assets and licenses, and review role-relevant reporting — without needing to coordinate every underlying tool or vendor themselves. That's the difference between a managed IT platform and a managed IT patchwork, and it's what makes scalable IT services and flexible IT solutions possible for businesses growing faster than their internal IT headcount.


## Rebutting the "complex and commodity" narrative around outsourced IT Services


Let's address the elephant in the room: for a lot of decision-makers, "outsourced IT services" still conjures images of generic, reactive support — a ticket goes in, someone gets back to you eventually, and you hope for the best. That perception isn't entirely unfair; plenty of the market still operates that way, bundling individual functions without any real orchestration layer underneath.


But that's precisely the definition[Xerox ITaaS](https://www.xerox.com/en-us/services/it-solutions/it-as-a-service) is built to move away from. We're not interested in being another generic IT service provider offering the same reactive, ticket-in-ticket-out experience as everyone else. Our platform brings managed IT expertise and a centralized, ServiceNow-built operating model together, so what you get isn't commodity outsourcing — it's a connected system that proactively identifies issues, routes them intelligently, and resolves what it can before it ever reaches your inbox.


Compare that with the fragmented-tools-plus-reactive-tickets model still common across much of the managed IT space, including among traditional players like Canon, Konica Minolta, and Ricoh. Their offerings do real work, and we're not here to say otherwise — but when every function sits in its own silo, the burden of coordination quietly shifts back onto you. Xerox ITaaS takes that coordination off your plate and puts it inside the platform, where AIOps can actually do something useful with it.


Cost deserves the same straight talk. Where fragmented providers stack per-function contracts and surprise overage fees, Xerox ITaaS consolidates spend into one predictable, scalable model — so IT cost management stops being a quarterly guessing game and starts being something you can actually plan around.


## Frequently asked questions


###


Is ITaaS the same as managed IT services?


### Is ITaaS the same as managed IT services?


Not quite. Managed IT services typically describe individual functions — device support, network monitoring, help desk — delivered separately. ITaaS is the operating model that brings those functions together under one continuous lifecycle and one centralized, AI-powered platform, so they work as a system rather than a stack of standalone contracts.


###


What is an ITaaS platform?


### What is an ITaaS platform?


An ITaaS platform is the technology layer — in our case, built on ServiceNow — that coordinates procurement, provisioning, support, and optimization in one place. It's what turns IT infrastructure management from a set of disconnected tools into a single, orchestrated environment with one view of what's happening across your business.


###


How does AIOps support ITaaS?


### How does AIOps support ITaaS?


AIOps is the engine behind the platform's proactive IT support. It uses anomaly detection to catch issues early, intelligent ticket routing to get problems to the right resource without manual triage, and automated remediation to resolve common issues without waiting on a technician — reducing manual effort at every stage of the ITaaS lifecycle.


###


Can ITaaS work with an internal IT team?


### Can ITaaS work with an internal IT team?


Yes. Xerox ITaaS is built to extend an internal team's capacity, not replace it. Automated remediation and intelligent routing absorb the repetitive, high-volume work, freeing your team to focus on strategic IT resource management and projects that need a human decision-maker.


###


What can users manage through the ITaaS portal?


### What can users manage through the ITaaS portal?


Through the centralized ITaaS portal, users can view IT health and service status, submit and track tickets, access self- service resources, manage assets and licenses, and pull role-relevant reporting — all from one place, without chasing multiple vendors or dashboards.


###


How does ITaaS help growing businesses?


### How does ITaaS help growing businesses?


As businesses add users, sites, and devices, fragmented support models break down fastest. ITaaS is designed for IT scalability from the outset, with flexible IT solutions and a predictable cost structure that grow with you, rather than requiring a new vendor or contract every time your footprint changes.


## What easier management actually looks like


The usability question — is ITaaS actually easier to manage? — isn't going to be settled by marketing language. It's settled by whether a platform can show its work: structured lifecycle stages, visible automation mechanics, and a single portal that replaces the spreadsheet-and-vendor-call juggling act most growing businesses are tired of.


That's what we've built with Xerox IT as a Service. Operational clarity, proactive IT support, reduced manual burden, scalable IT services, predictable IT cost management, and better-informed decisions — these aren't abstract ITaaS benefits, they're the direct outcomes of anomaly detection, intelligent ticket routing, and automated remediation working together inside one AI-powered, ServiceNow-built platform.


If you're managing fragmented vendors, a stretched IT team, or technology needs that have outgrown your current setup, it's worth finding out what a genuinely orchestrated approach looks like for your business.
